summary.title: A muscle map you need
points: About ten big groups: chest, shoulders, biceps, abdominals, quadriceps on the front.
Upper back, lats, triceps, glutes, hamstrings, calves on the back.
Most muscle mass sits in the legs, hips and back.
Muscles work in teams; plan movements and the muscles come with them.

exercises.scenario: Your weekly routine: push-ups, curls, crunches and running.

questions.prompt: Which big groups get no strength work?
options: Chest and triceps, since push-ups only train the shoulders
questions.explanation: Most of your muscle mass is untrained.

questions.prompt: Why start a programme from legs, hips and back?
options: Arms can't be trained at home
They're the biggest groups and carry the heaviest loads
They're the easiest muscles to grow with light dumbbells
questions.explanation: More muscle per session, more energy used.

exercises.scenario: A friend asks which muscles a push-up trains.

questions.prompt: Best answer?
options: Only the chest, since that's the main muscle in the movement
Chest, front of shoulders and triceps, with the abs holding the body straight

questions.prompt: Where are the hamstrings?
options: Front of the thighs, above the knee
questions.explanation: The quadriceps are at the front.

summary.title: Movement patterns
points: Seven patterns: squat, hinge, lunge, push, pull, carry, rotate or resist rotation.
Squat: knees and hips bend together. Hinge: hips go back, slight knee bend.
Carry: walking with weight. Rotate: turning, or resisting being twisted.
A full-body week touches every pattern; two sessions can share them out.
A teaching model: coaches' lists vary.

exercises.scenario: You map your current circuit: goblet squats, push-ups, curls, crunches.

questions.prompt: Which patterns are missing?
options: Squat and push, which are the two most important patterns
None; curls count as a pull
questions.explanation: Curls are isolation, not a pulling pattern.

questions.prompt: Which pattern is a farmer's carry?
options: Hinge, because you pick the weights up from the floor

exercises.scenario: A coach lists 'push, pull, hinge, squat, carry' and leaves out lunges.

questions.prompt: Is that wrong?
options: No: lists vary; it's a teaching model
Yes: lunges are the most important pattern
Yes: the seven-pattern list is an official guideline
questions.explanation: The point is covering the body, not the exact list.

questions.prompt: Which exercise is a hinge?
options: Goblet squat with an upright torso
questions.explanation: Driven by the hips moving back and forward.

summary.title: Push and pull directions
points: Horizontal push (push-up), vertical push (overhead press).
Horizontal pull (row), vertical pull (pull-up, pulldown).
Aim for roughly as many pulling sets as pushing sets: a convention, not a law.
Pushing is easy to overdo at home because push-ups need no kit.
Without a bar: rows, plus a high-anchored band for the vertical pull.

exercises.scenario: Your week has 9 sets of push-ups and 3 sets of rows.

questions.prompt: What's the fix?
options: Add rows until pulling sets are about equal
Drop push-ups entirely, since pushing causes shoulder injury

questions.prompt: Which pattern is missing with no pull-up bar?
options: Horizontal pull, since rows need a bench

exercises.scenario: Someone says 'unbalanced push and pull guarantees shoulder injury'.

questions.prompt: What does the lesson say?
options: It's proven: any imbalance causes injury within a year
Evidence for injury is limited; balance is sensible practice
questions.explanation: Treat it as practice, not law.

questions.prompt: Which is a vertical push?
options: Push-up on the floor with hands under the shoulders

summary.title: Knee-dominant vs hip-dominant
points: Knee-dominant: knees forward, bend a lot; quadriceps work most (squats).
Hip-dominant: hips back, shins near vertical; glutes and hamstrings work most (hinges).
Lunges and step-ups sit in between.
Put one of each in every session.
Hinges outgrow a light kettlebell first; swings and one-leg hinges help.

exercises.scenario: Session A: goblet squat and split squat. No hinge.

questions.prompt: What's undertrained?
options: Quadriceps, because split squats load the back leg

questions.prompt: Which exercise would you add?
options: Another goblet squat variation with a pause

exercises.scenario: Your 12 kg kettlebell feels light in deadlifts but hard in presses.

questions.prompt: Why?
options: Deadlifts are an isolation exercise, so they need less load
Glutes and hamstrings are far stronger than shoulders
The kettlebell weighs less when lifted from the floor

questions.prompt: What makes a light bell harder in a hinge?
options: Speed (swings) or one leg at a time
Holding the breath for the whole set

summary.title: One side or both
points: Bilateral: both sides together. Unilateral: one side at a time.
2021 meta-analysis: training carries over to the way you trained.
Two-sided training improved two-sided strength more; one-sided training improved one-legged jumps more.
No clear difference for sprint, change of direction or one-sided strength.
At home, one-sided work makes light weights harder and trains balance.

exercises.scenario: You have dumbbells up to 10 kg and want harder leg work.

questions.prompt: Which change helps most?
options: Do the same goblet squats with less rest between sets
Train legs only once a month
Switch to split squats or single-leg deadlifts
questions.explanation: One leg carries most of the load.

questions.prompt: What's the trade-off?
options: Each side needs its own set, so it takes longer
It can't be done with dumbbells
One-sided work builds no strength at all

exercises.scenario: A tennis player wants a better one-legged push-off.

questions.prompt: Which training fits best?
options: Only two-sided squats, which carry over best to one leg

questions.prompt: What did the meta-analysis find for sprinting?
options: A large advantage for two-sided training
A large advantage for one-sided training
questions.explanation: Small studies; treat as a guide.

summary.title: Free weights, machines, bodyweight
points: Free weights: you control the path. Machines: guided. Bodyweight: your body is the load.
2023 meta-analysis: no overall difference in muscle growth or jump height.
Strength gains were greatest on the kind of equipment trained with.
ACSM 2026: the choice makes no consistent difference for most healthy adults.
Free weights train stability; machines are easiest to push to failure safely.

exercises.scenario: You train only with dumbbells and kettlebells at home.

questions.prompt: Compared with gym machines, what can you expect?
options: Much less muscle growth, because machines isolate muscles better

questions.prompt: Where will your strength show most?
options: On machine tests at the gym
questions.explanation: Strength is specific to the equipment trained with.

exercises.scenario: A friend says 'you can't build muscle without machines'.

questions.prompt: What does the evidence say?
options: Machines are required for anyone over 40
Bodyweight builds more muscle than any weight
Free weights, bodyweight and bands work as well for muscle

questions.prompt: Which is a real advantage of machines?
options: Easier to learn and safer to push to failure
They build more muscle per set than free weights

summary.title: Compound vs isolation
points: Compound: several joints and muscles (squat, row, press, swing).
Isolation: one joint, one muscle (curl, lateral raise, calf raise).
In short studies of beginners, adding arm isolation added little.
Isolation suits side shoulders and calves, finishers and spare time.
Build sessions from 4–5 compound exercises.

exercises.scenario: You have 30 minutes and want fat loss and muscle.

questions.prompt: Which plan uses the time best?
options: Curls, triceps extensions, lateral raises, calf raises

questions.prompt: When do curls earn a place?
options: First, to warm up the biceps for rows
At the end, if time allows
questions.explanation: Isolation is the first thing to drop.

exercises.scenario: A beginner asks whether they need separate arm exercises to grow their arms.

questions.prompt: What did short beginner studies find?
options: Little or no extra benefit at first
A large extra benefit from the very first week of training
questions.explanation: One found slightly more arm size.

questions.prompt: Which muscle do compound moves train less?
options: The glutes, which only isolation work can reach

summary.title: Muscles and patterns
points: Ten muscle groups; most mass in legs, hips and back.
Plan with seven patterns: squat, hinge, lunge, push, pull, carry, rotate or resist.
Push and pull in two directions; keep sets roughly balanced.
One knee-dominant and one hip-dominant exercise in every session.
Without a bar, rows and a high band cover pulling.

exercises.scenario: You redesign your circuit of push-ups, curls, crunches and goblet squats.

questions.prompt: Which three patterns do you add first?
options: Push, squat and rotation, since they're already working well

questions.prompt: Which exercise covers the hinge with your kit?
options: Goblet squat with an upright torso

questions.prompt: Explain why planning by patterns beats planning by body parts.
questions.modelAnswer: Muscles work in teams, so movements train several groups at once. Covering every pattern each week makes sure every big muscle group is trained, without counting muscles.

exercises.scenario: Your weekly sets: push 10, pull 3, squat 6, hinge 0.

questions.prompt: What are the two main gaps?
options: Pushing and squatting, which need more volume

questions.prompt: Which muscles does the missing hinge leave undertrained?

summary.title: Choosing exercises
points: Training carries over to the way you trained: two-sided or one-sided.
One-sided work makes light weights harder and helps balance.
Free weights and machines build similar muscle; strength is equipment-specific.
Compound exercises first; isolation if time allows.
Home kit plus bodyweight and bands can build as much muscle as a gym.

exercises.scenario: You pick 5 exercises for a 30-minute home session with 10 kg dumbbells and a 12 kg bell.

questions.prompt: Which list fits best?
options: Curl, lateral raise, triceps extension, calf raise, crunch
Split squat, kettlebell RDL, push-up, one-arm row, swing

questions.prompt: Why split squats rather than goblet squats here?
options: One leg carries more, so the light load works harder
Split squats need no balance at all
Goblet squats don't train the legs

questions.prompt: Name one advantage each for free weights and for machines.
questions.modelAnswer: Free weights: train stability and carry over to real-life lifting; home-friendly. Machines: easier to learn and safer to push to failure.

exercises.scenario: A gym-goer says your home training is 'second best'.

questions.prompt: What does the 2023 meta-analysis say?
options: Home training is only for endurance
Similar muscle growth; strength shows on what you trained with
Machines always build more muscle and strength

questions.prompt: When would you add isolation work?
options: If the session has time after the compound lifts
questions.explanation: It's the first thing to drop when time is short.

summary.title: Movement patterns: the whole picture
points: Ten muscle groups; legs, hips and back hold most of the muscle.
Seven patterns cover the body: squat, hinge, lunge, push, pull, carry, rotate.
Balance push and pull, and knee- and hip-dominant work.
One-sided work suits light kit and sport.
Free weights and bodyweight build as much muscle as machines.
Compound exercises first; isolation if there's time.

exercises.scenario: You write session A for a 30-minute full-body week.

questions.prompt: Which structure fits?
options: Chest and triceps today, back and biceps another day
A squat, a hinge, a push, a pull, plus a carry or core move

questions.prompt: Which pull fits without a bar?
options: Pull-up from a door frame you haven't bought yet

questions.prompt: Where do curls go?
options: At the end, if time allows

exercises.scenario: Your old routine was the same circuit every week, mostly push-ups and squats.

questions.prompt: What does Module 2 change most?
options: Covering every pattern with balanced push–pull and squat–hinge
Adding a machine membership so the muscles can be isolated

questions.prompt: Which muscle groups will now get much more work?
Describe a balanced full-body session in one sentence, by pattern.
questions.modelAnswer: One squat (goblet or split squat), one hinge (Romanian deadlift or swing), one push (push-up or press), one pull (row), and a carry or core exercise, mostly compound moves.
